claims.text: The hypothesis concerns temperature-dependent stacking-fault energy in fcc Fe-Co-Ni-based high-entropy alloys.
Magnetic entropy arising from longitudinal spin fluctuations is the primary determinant of temperature-dependent stacking-fault energy.
Conventional static electronic-structure calculations cannot capture thermally induced magnetic moments on Co, Cr, and Ni.
Failure to capture thermally induced moments leads to inaccurate stacking-fault-energy predictions.
Failure to capture thermally induced moments causes misinterpretation of deformation mechanisms such as twinning.
The relevant initial state is a paramagnetic fcc Fe-Co-Ni-based high-entropy alloy at 50–1200 K.
Longitudinal-spin-fluctuation theory should replace the conventional floating-spin approach when calculating magnetic entropy and internal-energy contributions.
The calculations cover Wigner-Seitz radii of approximately 2.62–2.68 Bohr.
Longitudinal spin fluctuations thermally induce sizable magnetic moments on Co, Cr, and Ni atoms that have zero or small moments in static calculations.
The induced moments alter magnetic-entropy and internal-energy contributions to free energy.
Changes in magnetic contributions to free energy modify the calculated stacking-fault energy.
Stacking-fault energy increases with temperature because of magneto-volume coupling.
Increasing stacking-fault energy suppresses the formation of stacking faults and nano-twins.
Including longitudinal spin fluctuations yields a lower calculated stacking-fault-energy magnitude than floating-spin calculations at the same temperature.
The longitudinal-spin-fluctuation treatment correctly predicts suppression of stacking faults and nano-twinning at elevated temperatures up to 1000 K.
The temperature-dependent increase in stacking-fault energy is driven by magnetic entropy.
Floating-spin calculations overestimate the stacking-fault-energy magnitude.
The proposed mechanism is specific to the paramagnetic state, and explicit phonon effects are omitted.
The effect is most pronounced in systems containing Co, Cr, and Ni.
Assuming a constant interfacial energy introduces an error bar into stacking-fault-energy results.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and predicted outcome assign primary causation of the temperature-dependent SFE increase to magnetic entropy, whereas the mechanism field attributes that increase to magneto-volume coupling. These effects could coexist, but their relative causal roles are not reconciled.
